history.dynasty: Chola; built by Emperor Rajaraja I (reigned 985-1014 CE)
history.period: 1003-1010 CE; consecrated 1010 CE; fortified walls added after the 16th century
history.summary: The archetypal Great Chola temple and a UNESCO World Heritage Site (inscribed 1987) as part of the 'Great Living Chola Temples'. Called Rajarajesvaram by its builder, its 66-metre (216 ft) vimana was among the tallest structures of its age, built entirely of granite. The sanctum holds a huge monolithic lingam, and a 16-ft monolithic Nandi sits at the entrance. The walls carry Chola inscriptions documenting the temple's endowments and the empire's administration, plus famous Chola frescoes. The temple turned 1000 years old in 2010.

name: Brihadeeswarar Temple
town_description: Thanjavur (Tanjore) is the historic Chola capital on the south bank of the Cauvery in Thanjavur district. Beyond the Big Temple it holds the Thanjavur Palace, Saraswathi Mahal Library and a living tradition of bronze casting and Tanjore painting.
